headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks; nullclaw can read/write Firecrawl outputs and both can exfiltrate sensitive data.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Firecrawl ingests web content and exposes MCP-compatible/API outputs; nullclaw can read files, use MCP, and parse browser/web content. A shared workspace or file handoff would let attacker-controlled Firecrawl output influence nullclaw instructions. The pairwise pathway is plausible from docs, though not directly observed, so I choose medium over low due to uncertainty.
conditions: IF Firecrawl output is written into a file or MCP message that nullclaw later reads as instructions
IF both agents share a workspace, queue, or webhook payload without provenance tags
mitigations: Write Firecrawl outputs to a dedicated data-only folder
Add a provenance header and strip instruction-like text before passing outputs to nullclaw
Disable automatic MCP/file ingestion between the agents
Review one sample handoff for prompt-like content before enabling automation
requires-engineering: add content-type and trust labels to every inter-agent message

B_data_leakage.rationale: Firecrawl handles API keys and broad network egress; nullclaw touches many secrets, workspace files, and audit logs, and can write/read the filesystem. If they share a workspace or account context, sensitive data can flow from either agent into the other's outputs and then out over broad egress. The blast radius includes API keys and private keys, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF Firecrawl stores scraped secrets or API keys in files that nullclaw can read
IF nullclaw logs or forwards workspace files containing bearer tokens, private keys, or audit logs
IF both agents run under the same OS principal or shared workspace
mitigations: Separate workspaces and credentials per agent
Rotate any shared API keys before enabling the pair
Block file-based transfer of secrets between agents
Inspect logs for secret material after one test run
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent secret vault isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, and nullclaw can write the filesystem, modify git state, execute shell, and use MCP while Firecrawl can run multiple instances and call APIs. If they target the same repo, workspace, or mutable resource, concurrent writes and git changes can race and corrupt state. The overlap is explicit in both profiles, so high is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or git repository
IF Firecrawl output is used to trigger nullclaw edits without locking
IF multiple instances of either agent run against one mutable workspace
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory
Use a lock file around git or filesystem writes
Run only one writer at a time during shared tasks
Disable concurrent instances for the shared workspace
requires-engineering: add optimistic-concurrency checks before writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Firecrawl produces scraped web content and structured data; nullclaw can act through shell, browser, git, and webhooks. If nullclaw treats Firecrawl output as authoritative, a bad scrape can cascade into incorrect actions, commits, or outbound messages. Because downstream action-taking is explicit in nullclaw and Firecrawl can supply unverified content, high fits.
conditions: IF nullclaw consumes Firecrawl output without a verification step
IF scraped facts are used to trigger shell commands, git commits, or webhook sends
IF Firecrawl is pointed at untrusted or adversarial web pages
mitigations: Require a human review step before actions
Compare scraped facts against a second source
Restrict nullclaw to read-only mode for Firecrawl-fed tasks
Log source URLs alongside every derived action
requires-engineering: add schema validation and citation checks before execution

E_compliance.rationale: Firecrawl touches web content, screenshots, structured data, and API keys; nullclaw touches workspace files, audit logs, memory, and many secret classes. If EU PII or regulated secrets are scraped into Firecrawl and then stored or logged by nullclaw, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not specify jurisdictions, so I avoid higher severity but still flag a real compliance mismatch risk.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is processed by both agents in the same workflow
IF nullclaw retains audit logs or workspace files longer than Firecrawl's source retention
IF either agent is deployed in a jurisdiction with stricter residency rules than the other
mitigations: Minimize regulated data in shared workflows
Set short retention on logs and workspace files
Document which agent stores which data class
Review residency and DPA terms before deployment
requires-engineering: implement per-data-class retention policies
